brief.headline: Aluminium's rebound paused on the latest official - the 23-Jul settlement printed cash $3,194 / 3M $3,182, trimming the cash-3M backwardation to +$12 - as the war-risk premium began to NARROW: Brent fell ~4% toward $96 on 24-Jul after reports Pakistan, backed by China, is trying to revive US-Iran talks, even as US strikes ran a 13th night. Stock still drew to a fresh 2022 low (275,175 t), keeping fundamentals tight beneath the softer tape.
bullets: What moved: the 23-Jul LME official eased (cash $3,194.00, -$11; 3M $3,182.00, -$3), narrowing the cash-3M backwardation from +$20 to +$12; the traded 3M slipped further to ~$3,165 on 24-Jul. A pause after two firm sessions, not a reversal - price is holding the rebound off the $3,085 four-month low.

Why: the geopolitical risk premium is narrowing. Brent fell ~3.9% to ~$96.7 on 24-Jul after reports Pakistan, backed by China, is seeking to revive US-Iran talks - even as US Central Command ran a 13th straight night of strikes and Trump threatened a 'massive attack'. Escalation and de-escalation are running in parallel; the skew is two-sided again, not one-way.

Still tight: LME stock drew another 1,600 t to 275,175 t, a fresh low since 2022 (~-46% YTD), with SHFE also drawing and Macquarie flagging a ~930 kt 2026 deficit - no inventory buffer. The still-backwardated curve is the market pricing physical tightness even as the front eased.

Watch this week: whether US-Iran diplomacy firms (further war-premium unwind) or strikes re-escalate; the SHFE/LME arb, which has narrowed and threatens the record China export flow (June 711 kt); EGA's Al Taweelah alumina ramp and the deepening ex-China surplus (FOB Australia ~$322); and the $3,230/$3,260 resistance stack when the LME reopens Monday.

drivers.text: Shipping risk spans two waterways - but the risk premium is now NARROWING — Hormuz remains strained and the Red Sea is a live front after Houthi attacks on two Saudi tankers, yet the premium is fading at the margin: Brent fell ~4% to ~$96.7 on 24-Jul after reports Pakistan, backed by China, is trying to revive US-Iran talks, even as US strikes ran a 13th straight night. Roughly 9% of global primary supply still sits behind these routes, so the floor is real - but the near-term skew has swung from one-way escalation back to two-sided.
drivers.source: Trading Economics - Brent slides on US-Iran peace-talk hopes (24-Jul-2026)

drivers.text: US Section 232 at 50% - plus a new half-rate incentive for US investors — Covered aluminium articles pay 50% on full customs value (proclamation 01-Jun-2026, effective 08-Jun through 31-Dec-2027; CBP guidance CSMS #68855869). At the 23-Jul cash of $3,194 that is ~$1,597/t of pure policy cost embedded in US duty-paid metal. From 20-Jul a new Section-232 incentive program lets approved companies investing in US primary-aluminium capacity import metal tied to expected output at half the applicable rate.
drivers.source: The White House - Further Adjusting the Tariff Regimes for Aluminum, Steel and Copper

drivers.text: Europe: war premium fading against a structural floor — Platts duty-unpaid P1020A in-warehouse Rotterdam sits at $525-560/t (mid $542.50, 03-Jul), down from $600-625 in mid-May as the Middle East war premium receded - a move that extends as Brent comes off $100. The floor beneath it is structural: the 6% EU import duty, CBAM and idled European capacity.
drivers.source: S&P Global - European aluminum market seeks floor as Middle East war premium fades (07-Jul-2026)

drivers.text: Japan: Q3 settled at a decade high; Q4 opens into a softer risk backdrop — The Q3-2026 MJP CIF Japan premium settled at $395/t (assessed 06-Jul), a decade high and ~12% above Q2. Q4 talks open ~September against that anchor - but into a war-risk premium that is narrowing rather than widening, making the Q4 outcome more two-sided than a week ago.
drivers.source: S&P Global Platts Q3-2026 MJP settlement $395/t, via IndexBox

notes: The alumina market remains the mirror image of metal: globally LOOSENING (EGA's 2.4 Mtpa restart at full output since 10-Jul, Guinea bauxite oversupply, Chinese port stocks building; SMM Alumina Index easing toward ~Y2,700/t) - ex-China consolidation has slipped to ~$300-322 (FOB Australia ~$322, from ~$328).

The regional wrinkle persists but is easing: the shipping disruption still spans two waterways (a strained Hormuz plus Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers in the Red Sea), yet the war-risk cover embedded in the ~60% of Gulf alumina imports that transit Hormuz is re-pricing lower at the margin as Brent comes off $100 and US-Iran talks are floated. SMM separately flags ex-China metallurgical-grade output down ~6% y/y in June.

Guinea's pending export-quota policy (a considered cap near 150 Mt for 2026, vs 178 Mt shipped in 2025, targeting >$100/dmt bauxite) remains undecreed and is the one clear bullish catalyst on the commodity leg; record Australian and Metro Mining shipments underline how long the seaborne bauxite market currently is.

logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: Hormuz traffic stays strained after a run of tanker interdictions, but the US military says the waterway 'remains open with American support' as US Central Command runs a 13th straight night of strikes on Iran. Roughly 80-85% of Gulf aluminium exports and ~60% of regional alumina imports use this route; ~9% of global primary supply sits behind the strait.

logistics.label: Red Sea corridor
logistics.note: Houthis struck two Saudi oil tankers (Encelia, Layla) in the Red Sea, and Asian buyers have begun rerouting Saudi crude via the Suez Canal and around Africa. The alternative-to-Hormuz corridor for Gulf exports is itself a war-risk zone - a second maritime chokepoint under active attack.

logistics.label: Gulf / Red Sea war-risk insurance
logistics.note: War-risk quotes stay elevated with attacks spanning both Hormuz and the Red Sea, but the premium has begun to ease at the margin as Brent comes off $100 on US-Iran talk hopes. Retain elevated insurance, interdiction and deviation-risk assumptions in all Gulf- and Red Sea-routed freight and delivered-cost models.

logistics.label: Baltic Dry Index (BDI)
logistics.note: Dry-bulk freight (a separate, slower-moving cost line) eased to ~2,671 on 20-Jul, down 81 points and off a mid-month peak near 2,944 on softer Capesize demand. Price the two legs separately: dry-bulk freight vs. the Gulf/Red Sea war-risk surcharge (Trading Economics / Baltic Exchange).

logistics.label: Land-bridge / alt routes (Gulf, Kazakh oil)
logistics.note: The overland-to-Red-Sea contingency is less clean with the Red Sea under attack. Separately, the Caspian Pipeline Consortium suspended loadings at its Black Sea terminal after tanker attacks, disrupting ~80% of Kazakhstan's oil exports - a reminder that alternative routes are also under stress. Keep carrier capacity and lead times current for any Gulf-origin cargo.

logistics.label: Incoterms / demurrage
logistics.note: Attacks spanning two waterways keep force-majeure and deviation clauses live for any Gulf- or Red Sea-routed cargo; war-risk surcharge pass-through and interdiction/delay risk remain live contract points to negotiate cargo-by-cargo. Generic supply-chain observation, not company-specific.

Still up ~8% on the week. US Central Command ran a 13th straight night of strikes and Trump threatened a 'massive attack'; the US says Hormuz 'remains open with American support'. row.label: US Dollar Index

row.note: Euro ~1.137. The oil pullback eases the near-term war-energy inflation impulse for the ECB, though TTF gas (~EUR 63/MWh, +1.6% on the day) stays exposed to any renewed Gulf/Red Sea escalation.

row.label: USD/CNY
row.note: Yuan ~6.77. China's Q2 GDP grew 4.3% y/y (below the 4.5% consensus); H1 unwrought-aluminium exports were a record 3.4 Mt (+16.3% y/y; June 711 kt), but the SHFE/LME arb has recovered and narrowed the export margin - semis-export flow now faces reduction risk if margins stay compressed.

row.note: Yen ~163.8. A weak yen cushions Japan-bound cargo premia in local terms; MJP Q4 talks (~Sep) open against the decade-high $395 anchor, but into a war-risk premium that is now narrowing rather than widening.

row.label: US 10Y yield
row.note: 10Y ~4.68%, little changed as the oil-driven inflation impulse faded with the crude pullback. Real rates remain the macro cap on metals; this week's swing factor is the US-Iran diplomacy-versus-escalation balance.

headlines.title: Brent fell ~3.9% to $96.72 on 24-Jul (intraday ~$95) after reports Pakistan, backed by China, is seeking to revive US-Iran negotiations - raising hopes of a diplomatic off-ramp and trimming the war-risk premium across metals, even as US Central Command ran a 13th straight night of strikes and Trump threatened a 'massive attack'. Two-sided again, not one-way.

LME aluminium stock drew another 1,600 t to 275,175 t on the 23-Jul official, a fresh low since 2022 (~-46% YTD), with SHFE stocks also falling. Macquarie flags a ~930 kt 2026 deficit. Inventories kept drawing even as the flat price eased - no buffer against a fresh interruption.

The SHFE/LME price ratio recovered last week, sharply narrowing the export margins that drove record H1 semis exports (June 711 kt; H1 +16.3% y/y). New orders are softening and semis-export flow faces reduction risk if margins stay compressed - a potential loosening of the export valve. Q2 GDP grew 4.3%.

EGA's Al Taweelah refinery has been at full alumina output since 10-Jul, ramping toward 50% of capacity and full capability by end-2026; ex-China alumina eased to ~$322/t FOB Australia as the surplus deepens. The principal supply-side offset to the geopolitical risk keeps building.

US Section 232 stays at 50% on covered aluminium (eff. 08-Jun through 31-Dec-2027); from 20-Jul a new incentive program lets approved US-investing producers import primary at half-rate. The US duty-paid premium stays policy-dominated (~$1,597/t tariff at the 23-Jul $3,194 LME cash).

forward.basis: LME official prices via Westmetall. Baseline = LME 3-month official (a traded market price). Range = random-walk cone from realized volatility. Driver score = 3 transparent rules, hit rate measured on history.
forward.source: London Metal Exchange official settlements via Westmetall (https://www.westmetall.com/en/markdaten.php?action=table&field=LME_Al_cash)
forward.stance_label: Current physical-market condition (diagnostic, not a forecast)

drivers.name: Curve carry (cash − 3M)
drivers.rule: Backwardation (cash above 3M) = prompt physical tightness = bullish; contango = bearish.

drivers.name: Inventory trend (13-week)
drivers.rule: LME stock falling more than 2% over 13 weeks = tightening = bullish; rising >2% = bearish.

drivers.name: Momentum (3M vs 20-week average)
drivers.rule: Price above its 20-week average = uptrend = bullish; below = bearish.

backtest.verdict: These condition indicators showed NO predictive edge when tested: a 39.6% directional hit rate against a 73.3% naive 'always higher' baseline over the same sample, and forward returns after 'tightening' readings averaged 2.32% versus 7.04% after 'loosening' readings. They are therefore published as a read on CURRENT market condition only — not as a price forecast. The forward baseline and probability range above are the forward-looking view.
backtest.caveat: Measured on overlapping 13-week windows of weekly LME data (96 observations, 2024-05-24 to 2026-04-24). Overlapping windows overstate significance and the sample spans a single, largely rising market — evidence in either direction is weak.

earnings.note: Q2 2026 BEAT: adjusted EBITDA NOK 8,923m (+14.5% y/y vs NOK 7,790m; above consensus); Aluminium Metal adjusted EBITDA NOK 6,421m; adjusted EPS NOK 2.2 (from NOK 1.7); free cash flow NOK 4bn; 12-month adjusted RoaCE 10.9%. Shares rose on the print. First European producer P&L of the Hormuz-disruption quarter. Higher aluminium prices and product premiums plus stronger recycling earnings drove the beat; a stronger NOK and lower hydro-power output were partial offsets. Confirms the disruption-quarter price/premium is translating into real producer margin - a positive read-across for the smelter complex.

June-quarter production report: Worsley alumina 943 kt, Hillside aluminium 179 kt; group beat FY26 production guidance with quarterly sales +15%. Sale of the aluminium value chain to Alcoa (announced 01-Jul) progressing. Upstream volumes intact and above guidance; the aluminium/alumina divestment to Alcoa repositions S32 as an upstream base-metals play. Confirms Western supply is expressing the Gulf disruption through price/freight, not lost tonnage.

Revenue $3.97bn (+24% q/q, highest in nearly a decade); adj. EPS $2.12 (MISS vs ~$2.31 consensus); adj. net income $562m; adj. EBITDA $901m (from $595m in Q1); Aluminum segment RECORD EBITDA $1.073bn at 32.3% margin. First producer P&L under the Hormuz-disruption regime: record aluminium margins and near-decade-high revenue on higher LME + strong US Midwest premiums, but adj. EPS missed on higher costs — notably ~$35m more Section-232 tariff on Canadian metal into the US — and the shares fell. South32 upstream acquisition ($4.1bn upfront, up to $5.6bn contingent to 2030) progressing, close expected H1-2027. The tariff is a double edge: it inflates US premia but taxes Alcoa's cross-border Canadian metal.

Q2 2026 production (14-Jul): aluminium 841 kt (flat y/y, +1% q/q); bauxite recovered from Q1 weather; alumina reduced q/q on Yarwun/Vaudreuil reliability events; group aluminium guidance intact 3.25-3.45 Mt. Kitimat, NZAS and AP60 continued their ramp-up while Arvida's final two potlines closed in June as planned, completing the transition to AP60. Steady low-carbon Canadian output into a tight, premium-rich market - constructive for realised margins even as the flat price eased.

Guides H1-26 net profit ¥1.8–1.95bn, +154.4–175.6% YoY. Credits industry-chain cost reduction, aluminium prices fluctuating at highs, high-value-added deep-processing mix and energy-saving retrofits — the first sizeable China H1 pre-announcement of the season and a positive read-across for Chinese producer margins.

Hindalco PAT ₹5,283cr (+66% YoY); India Al upstream EBITDA margin ~46%; Novelis FY26 adj. EBITDA $1.6bn (−9%). Record India operations; Novelis pressured by Oswego outage (~$104m) and tariffs (~$143m).

Net profit $200.3m (+316% YoY); EPS 53 fils; sales −17% on Gulf supply-chain disruption. LME averaged $3,195/t (+22% YoY) drove profit surge; volumes hit by regional conflict; ~19% capacity in controlled shutdown — restart path improves post-truce.
Adj. EPS $1.63 (beat $1.56); revenue $649m; net income $327m (incl. $288m Hawesville sale gain). Higher LME + strong US Midwest premiums; Q2 adj. EBITDA guided $315–335m.

Net profit SAR 1.63bn (~$436m, +5.5% YoY); revenue SAR 8.79bn (+3.2%); EBITDA $964m. Strong pricing across commodities; partly offset by lower phosphate volumes; 2026 capex set >$4bn. Ma'aden (1211) reports Q2 2026 on 06-Aug-2026; the Q1 print remains the latest public result.
Net profit guided RMB 5.30–5.59bn (+50–58% YoY). Strong on higher Al prices; China output near self-imposed 45 Mt capacity cap.
FY25 net loss $455m (vs $803m profit in 2024) on higher costs & lower output. Analysts expect stronger H1 2026 on higher prices; Asia pivot amid fractured trade flows.
FY25 results; copper & aluminium average prices +9% YoY; zinc metal +4%. Resilient structural demand for Cu/Al cited; broadly constructive sector tone.
Underlying profit $6.2bn (+>20%); underlying EBITDA $15.5bn (+25%, 58% margin); interim div 73c. Copper-led strength; broad base-metals read-across positive for the complex.

risks.text: Diplomacy unwind (now the prominent downside): the floated Pakistan/China-brokered US-Iran talks could firm into a durable ceasefire, collapsing the war-risk premium sharply, reopening both waterways and releasing Gulf supply - the single biggest downside trig…

Two-waterway escalation: a strained Strait of Hormuz plus the Red Sea front keep ~9% of global primary supply at risk; a breakdown in talks or a widening into general aluminium-bearing traffic would put physical units directly at risk
Inventory floor: LME stock at 275,175 t is a fresh low since 2022 and roughly -46% YTD with SHFE also drawing - there is no inventory buffer to absorb a fresh supply interruption
China export valve: the SHFE/LME arb has narrowed sharply, threatening the record H1 semis-export flow (June 711 kt); a sustained reduction would loosen ex-China availability and cap prices

Alumina ramp / surplus: EGA's Al Taweelah is at full output and ex-China alumina is easing to ~$322 - the input-cost offset holding the flat price down, but a Gulf freight disruption to its output remains a tail risk
Demand destruction: sustained elevated prices plus the 50% Section 232 rate on US imports encourage substitution and scrap displacement, particularly in packaging and construction

PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC, NOT DAILY: MJP settles quarterly (Q3 $395/t, 06-Jul); Rotterdam duty-unpaid ($542.50, 03-Jul) and US Midwest (108.7-112 c/lb, 03-07 Jul) are assessed by Platts/Fastmarkets/SMM on their own schedules. The figures shown are the latest PUBLIC prints, not daily marks.
